text: The adjoint method is the engine of inverse design because it computes the gradient of an objective F with respect to every design variable using how many electromagnetic simulations?
choices: One simulation per design variable (finite differences)
Two simulations — one forward, one adjoint — with cost independent of the number of design variables
N simulations, one per wavelength, then averaged
A single forward simulation, from which all gradients read off directly
explanation: The adjoint method gets dF/d-epsilon at every point from just a forward run and an adjoint run (same solver, source at the output monitor), with cost independent of the number of variables — which is what lets an optimizer tune 10^5 pixels. Choice 0 is the finite-difference cost the adjoint method avoids; choice 2 confuses wavelength sampling with the gradient; choice 3 is wrong — one forward run alone cannot yield the gradient without the adjoint solve.
